common_name: Regal Shields Alocasia (Silver-Sheened Shield-Leaf Elephant Ear)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants after all frost danger has passed, in rich, well-drained but moisture-retentive soil in partial to full shade; in zone 9 the rhizome often survives mild winters with heavy mulch, but lift and store indoors where hard freezes are possible.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Regal Shields is a bold hybrid Alocasia grown for its enormous, thick, shield-shaped leaves in deep bronze-green with a distinctive matte, silvery-blue sheen and prominent dark veining, standing upright on sturdy stems for strong architectural presence in a shade bed or large container. It grows considerably larger and tougher-leaved than many Alocasia hybrids, tolerating more sun and wind than typical elephant ears without leaf tatter, which makes it a strong choice for a shaded patio focal point or as a dramatic centerpiece among smaller shade perennials. Keep soil evenly moist through the growing season and feed regularly for maximum leaf size, and where winters bring hard freezes, dig the rhizome before frost and store it dry and cool until spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions or corms after all frost danger has passed once soil is warm; Mojito grows quickly in zone 9's hot, humid summers and appreciates heavy mulch or lifting for storage where winters bring hard freezes.

directions: Plant in moist to wet, fertile soil in partial shade to shade, or full sun with abundant water; Mojito is a striking taro cultivar with bright lime-green, heart-shaped leaves irregularly splashed and speckled with purple-black blotches, giving each leaf a unique, painterly pattern reminiscent of the drink for which it is named. It is a fast, vigorous grower that quickly forms a substantial clump through a Gulf Coast summer, providing the same bold tropical texture as green elephant ear but with far more visual interest up close. Keep the soil consistently moist to wet through active growth, since colocasia is one of the more water-demanding tropical foliage plants, and where winters bring hard freezes either mulch heavily over the corm or dig and store it dry indoors.
